amendments.normalized_body: In `JsonLinesSink::emit_tick` and `StderrSink::emit_tick` (tracing.rs:124-128, 135-139), both serialization errors (`serde_json::to_string`) and write errors (`writeln!`) are silently swallowed. For CI archival use — one of the three stated output modes — silently losing trace records makes it impossible to detect data loss. At minimum, consider logging or counting dropped records. For `JsonLinesSink` specifically, the `let _ = writeln!` could be changed to propagate or record the error, since file I/O failures during CI runs are not uncommon (disk full, broken pipe). Alternatively, change `TraceSink::emit_tick` to return a `Result` so callers can decide the policy.

The manual `Clone` implementation for `Engine` (engine.rs:42-51) silently drops the tracer by setting it to `None` in the clone. There is no documentation on this behavior — neither a doc comment on the `Clone` impl, nor a note on `enable_tracing`. Downstream beads that clone engines (e.g., for forking scenarios or speculative rollbacks) will silently lose their tracing configuration. Add a doc comment on the `Clone` impl explaining that tracer is not cloned because `Box<dyn TraceSink>` is not `Clone`, so callers must re-enable tracing on cloned engines.

The `PoolSnapshot::deltas_to` method (tracing.rs:227-245) uses `f64::EPSILON` (~2.2e-16) as the threshold for reporting pool changes. This is extremely sensitive — for pool values in typical simulation ranges (0.01 to 1000), even innocuous arithmetic like `x = x * 1.0` or reading/writing through an intermediate can produce rounding noise that exceeds this threshold. Consider using a relative-or-absolute threshold, e.g. `delta.abs() > 1e-12 || (delta / before_val).abs() > 1e-12`, to suppress sub-picogram noise while still catching real sub-microgram changes relevant to budget tracking.

Fix `SimTracer` so tick numbering is monotonic even after `drain_ticks()`. In `crates/tank_core/src/tracing.rs:336-345`, `tick_index` is derived from `self.ticks.len()`, so draining the in-memory buffer causes later ticks to restart at 0. A long-running harness that periodically drains memory will therefore emit duplicate tick ids in its JSONL stream even though the simulation kept advancing. Keep a separate counter for the next tick id instead of tying ids to the retained buffer length.

Expand detail tracing beyond the current hard-coded pool subset. `crates/tank_core/src/tracing.rs:154-220` snapshots only selected fields, but systems mutate other state that never appears in `pool_deltas`, for example `system:stability_tracker` updates `stability_tracker.instability_index` and the tracker baselines in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:96-123`, and `system:daily_shrimp` mutates reproductive state in `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:384-505`. At detail verbosity those stages can emit empty deltas even when they changed state, and `crates/tank_core/src/tracing.rs:92-94` then silently reports `0.0` for absent pools. Either trace all mutation-relevant state or surface unsupported pools explicitly instead of treating 'untracked' as 'unchanged'.

Preserve emitted event details in the trace schema instead of collapsing them to a count. `SystemTraceEntry` stores only `events_generated: usize` in `crates/tank_core/src/tracing.rs:61-68`, and the engine fills it from `event_log.len()` deltas in `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:450-458` and `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:505-513`. For stages like `system:daily_biofilter_maturity`, which can emit both `BiofilmMaturityIncrease` and `CycleProgressing` in one pass (`crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:370-390`), the JSONL trace cannot tell downstream consumers which event(s) actually fired. Store the emitted event kind/message/causes in each trace entry, not just a count.
